title: The Lantern on the Black Tide

slides.text: My lighthouse does not warn ships away from rocks. It stands on the obsidian cliffs where the mortal world ends, burning whale-oil mixed with starlight so the newly dead can find their way across the fog-choked sea. For three hundred winters, I have watched millions of pale paper skiffs drift outward into the silver dark, never once turning back.

Last night, a gale tore at the lantern glass, and the tide ran backward. Through my brass spyglass, I saw a solitary wooden rowboat fighting the current, heading toward the shore of the living. A woman in a salt-crusted cloak was pulling the oars until her spectral hands bled light, her eyes fixed fiercely on my tower.

When her keel scraped the black shingle below, I descended the stairs with my iron hook, bound by oath to push her back into eternity. She looked up at me and held out a tiny woolen blanket wrapped around a sleeping infant's soul. 'The fever took us both,' she gasped, pressing the child into my arms. 'Keep the light burning. Only one of us was meant to stay.'
